source.title: Denoising Autoregressive Representation Learning
source.authors: Ya-Zhe Li; J. Bornschein; Ting Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study measures whether pre-training validation loss is associated with downstream performance in image models, a conceptual test of downstream predictability rather than a test of language-model power laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites language-model scaling laws and concurrent work on image-model scaling, but those cited results are not this study's results. Its own relevant evidence is the validation-loss/ImageNet-accuracy comparison in Table 15; the authors say there are too few datapoints for statistically significant analysis.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (image ViTs pre-trained autoregressively on ImageNet), Appendix B.3/Table 15 pairs the study's own pre-training validation losses with fine-tuned ImageNet top-1 accuracy. This bears on V6 (downstream performance tracks pre-training loss). It is a small side analysis with no fit and no extrapolation. The study does not test V1–V5 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report that, for the standard ViT sizes and training lengths they trained, lower pre-training validation loss correlates with better ImageNet fine-tuning accuracy for both MSE and same-schedule diffusion loss. They say there are too few datapoints for a statistically significant analysis and present it as a direction for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains image ViT models and compares validation loss with ImageNet classification accuracy; it does not fit language-model loss scaling laws or test compute-optimal allocations.
record.problems: The authors say there are too few datapoints for statistically significant analysis. Table 15 does not identify the model size corresponding to each datapoint, and reports no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of held-out loss against parameters, data or compute.
No fitting on small runs and no extrapolation.
No fixed-parameter shape comparison. Decoder-depth ablations concern the patch decoder and downstream accuracy, not loss at fixed size.
Image models are used, but no power-law form is fitted or tested for loss vs scale.

No predictive fit or extrapolation of accuracy from loss. Only ImageNet fine-tuning accuracy is used. Language models are not covered. Only five points per objective, mixing epoch and model-size changes.
No exponents or fitting choices examined.

missing.what: Downstream ImageNet fine-tuning accuracy vs model size (ViT-B/L/H). MSE: 82.7/84.7/85.5; diffusion: 81.9/84.9/85.9. Accuracy rises with scale but there is no fit.
ImageNet accuracy vs pre-training epochs (100–800) for ViT-L16 under MSE and diffusion. This is the same data underlying most of Table 15.

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope label is dropped. Too few datapoints weakens the evidence but does not show a condition where V6 fails; that caveat is folded into the supports reason. The Table 15 points can be matched to Fig. 4 and Table 5: four ViT-L16 runs at 100/200/400/800 epochs plus one ViT-H14 at 800 epochs per objective. The record's stage field (800 epochs for all) is therefore wrong. The fine-tuning length is stated as 90 epochs for training-schedule and scaling studies. V6 is read here as not restricted to language models. If the phenomenon restricts V6 to LMs, all rows should be ['none'] and the finding moved to fits_no_version. The intro remark that masked-prediction pretraining loss is not a reliable downstream indicator is an unsupported cited claim, not a result.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit of held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or extrapolation to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling.
No comparison isolating architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Although the study uses image models, it does not test whether a power-law form holds in images or other training regimes.
Tests validation loss against ImageNet top-1 accuracy for the reported image models only; no predictive fit or extrapolation, and no other downstream tasks are tested in this analysis.
No analysis of scaling-law exponents, compute-optimal fits, or their sensitivity to fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Image ViTs (ViT-L16 at 100–800 epochs plus ViT-H14), ImageNet fine-tuning, both MSE and diffusion objectives
relationships.reason: Across r1–r5 and r6–r10, every decrease in validation loss coincides with higher top-1 accuracy. The evidence is weak: five points per objective, no fit, and authors say too few for significance.
relationships.display_finding: Every validation-loss decrease coincided with higher top-1 accuracy, although five observations per objective were insufficient to establish significance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
